Intellectyx, Inc

Software Engineer

This was a true startup-style build. Small team, high ambiguity, and a lot of ownership.

I was brought in to help turn a rough idea into a product leaders could demo and teams could use daily: an AI assistant that could answer questions from messy internal documents.

The Real Scenario

Imagine a team lead asking a simple question like: "What changed in our policy for enterprise clients last quarter?"

Before this product, that answer could take 30 to 60 minutes of searching through PDFs, notes, spreadsheets, and old docs.

The goal was to make that answer available in seconds, with clear references.

What I Owned

  • Designed and shipped the backend flow from file upload to final response.
  • Built ingestion pipelines for messy files (PDF, CSV, docs) where structure was inconsistent.
  • Implemented retrieval and response orchestration so answers were grounded, not guessed.
  • Added streaming responses so the product felt fast and alive while models were still thinking.
  • Worked directly with stakeholders to tune behavior based on real usage, not lab assumptions.

Scrappy Startup Moments

1. MVP pressure with unclear requirements

We did not have a perfect spec. We had business urgency.

I broke the build into practical milestones and shipped the smallest useful version first, then iterated quickly based on user pain points.

2. "Looks right" was not enough

At first, responses sounded good but were sometimes off-context.

I tightened retrieval rules, improved chunking quality, and made citations visible so users could trust what they saw.

3. Speed vs reliability tradeoff

Users wanted instant responses. Enterprise teams needed dependable responses.

I added async processing and fallback behavior so the product stayed responsive without becoming fragile.

Human Impact

  • Teams spent less time hunting for information and more time making decisions.
  • Non-technical users could ask plain-English questions and get actionable answers.
  • Leadership had a product they could confidently put in front of customers.

What I'd Build Next

  • Better quality scoring for answers before they are shown.
  • Role-aware responses based on team permissions and context.
  • Multi-step assistant workflows for repeated business tasks.
